_meta.engine: Honda K20Z3 (2006-2011 Civic Si, 2007-2010 Acura CSX Type-S)
_meta.rule: Every value below was read on a fetched page. null = not found on any reachable page. Nothing is estimated.
_meta.accessNotes: The main community sources for stock K-series lobe specs (k20a.org 'stock cam specs' t=76662 and 'CAMS: z1 vs z3 vs a2 vs itr vs 06 tsx', 8thcivic.com 'Mother of all camshafts thread' and 'Does anyone know the K20Z3's cylinder head/cam specs', clubrsx.com, honda-tech.com, hondata.com forum 'What are K20Z4 stock camshaft specs?') and web.archive.org were all blocked or unreachable from this environment (proxy CONNECT 403 / fetch error / robots). The Scribd service-manual copy only rendered a JavaScript error page. So stock lobe lift/duration/centreline numbers could NOT be confirmed.
_meta.camCodesNote: The caller's suggested codes (RRB intake for K20Z3; PRB/PRC for K20Z1) could not be verified on any fetched page; the codes appear only in titles of unreachable forum threads (e.g. clubrsx 'RRB/TSX intake cam and PRC exhaust cam?'). Treat as unconfirmed.

camCodes.note: Unconfirmed. Not found on any fetched page.

intakeLow.centerlineNote: Intake centreline is variable via VTC (50 deg range per Honda). No stock base-position value found.

intakeHigh.centerlineNote: Variable via VTC. Honda press kit: 'At high engine speeds, valve lift phase on the intake side is increased by five degrees and on the exhaust side by 10 degrees' -- Honda does not say relative to what (likely vs the previous-gen engine) and gives no absolute values.

exhaustLow.centerlineNote: Exhaust cam has no VTC on the K20Z3 (fixed phase). No stock centreline value found.

exhaustHigh.centerlineNote: See intakeHigh note on Honda's '10 degrees' exhaust phase statement.

notes: Honda 2006 Civic powertrains release (Si engine): the VTC actuator advances or retards the intake cam across a '50 degree range' (Honda does not say crank or cam degrees in that sentence).

Hondata FlashPro 'VTC tuning' help: VTC moves the intake cam 'over a range of 50 crank degrees'; 'The allowable cam angle range is from 0 to 45 or 0 to 50 degrees, depending on the calibration type.' Hondata N/A guidance: max advance just after VTEC engagement until ~6500-7000 rpm, then retard 'back around 25 degrees' to redline.
Wikipedia VTEC: K-series intake cam 'capable of advancing between 25 and 50 degrees, depending upon engine configuration'; phasing by 'a computer-controlled, oil-driven adjustable cam sprocket'.
Tegiwa (Genuine Honda 25 deg VTC gear): the 25 deg actuator 'is found on the K24A3'; '50 degrees is the maximum amount of movement from any stock actuator'.
Wikipedia K engine: K20Z3 has VTC on the intake cam only, not the exhaust.

vtecActuation.switchRpmNote: Honda: above 5,800 rpm the intake and exhaust valves use high-lift, long-duration cam profiles (K20Z3). Wikipedia K engine also lists VTEC engagement 5800 rpm for K20Z3/K20Z1/K20A2. Both intake and exhaust cams have three lobes per cylinder (Wikipedia VTEC).
vtecActuation.oilPressureNote: No authoritative figure found. Only a Link ECU forum post: 'A quick google says something about being a 50PSI switch, but yeah, grain of salt.' -- unverified, not used.

ecuConditions.rpm: Stock K20Z3 switch point 5800 rpm (Honda). Hondata: VTEC point is a 'VTEC window' varying with engine speed and load ('allows the VTEC point to move higher with lighter engine load'); KManager example 3800 rpm at 96 kPa MAP rising linearly to 5500 rpm at 30 kPa MAP (tuning example, not the stock calibration); guide limits: not below 2500 rpm on twin-cam engines, not above 6500 rpm.
ecuConditions.loadMap: Hondata 'VTEC pressure window' = minimum MAP for VTEC activation vs rpm (no stock values published).
ecuConditions.vehicleSpeed: Hondata: 'VTEC engage and disengage minimum speed is the minimum vehicle speed before VTEC will activate'; disengage speed lower than engage speed. No stock value.
ecuConditions.coolantTemp: Hondata: 'VTEC minimum coolant temperature is the minimum water temperature before VTEC will activate.' No stock value.
ecuConditions.oilPressureSwitch: Hondata KManager: 'For JDM engines and JDM ECUs disable the VTEC oil pressure sensor' (i.e. USDM ECUs monitor a VTEC oil pressure switch). Wikipedia VTEC: ECU 'takes account of engine oil pressure, engine temperature, vehicle speed, engine speed, and throttle position'.
ecuConditions.hysteresis: Wikipedia VTEC: 'The switch back from high- to low-rpm cams is set to occur at a lower engine speed than the switch up.'

vtecActuation.switchTimeNote: No published ms figure found. Honda patent US4901685 notes a delay from energising the solenoid valve to piston movement that depends on engine speed, oil temperature, oil pressure and battery voltage, but gives no number.
vtecActuation.pinEngagement: Pin can only slide when the rocker arms are aligned, i.e. while the cam is on its base circle (valve closed). Honda patent US4901685 (Honda Giken Kogyo): 'During an interval Ac when the valve is closed, the first rocker arm 8 is held at rest' with guide holes 'kept in axial registry'; second embodiment adds 'a timing plate 39 for controlling the timing of movement of the piston 36'. So each cylinder switches on its own next base-circle window, not all at once. (Generic Honda VTEC patent, not K20Z3-specific.)
vtecActuation.mechanism: ECU energises the VTEC solenoid; a spool valve directs oil pressure through the rocker shaft to a locking pin that locks the outer (low-lobe) rockers to the centre high-lift rocker; spring returns the pin when pressure is released (Honda VTEC release; Counterman).
vtecActuation.notes: Oil pressure threshold and switch time remain unconfirmed.

otherSources.note: Aftermarket K20/K24 cams that list K20Z3 fitment. None of these pages publish stock comparison numbers; listed only as context for what 'upgraded' looks like.

skunk2TunerStage3.notes: 1.7 rocker ratio; i-VTEC settings: small lobe 35 deg advance, big lobe 40 deg tapering to 30 deg; VTEC crossover 5500-6500 rpm; claimed +30-33 hp over factory

junK20A.note: JUN Type0 (bolt-on, works with VTC), K20A: IN primary 244 deg/8.2 mm, mid 304/12.2, secondary 240/7.5; EX 248/8.5, 304/11.8, 244/7.8

brianCrowerStage2FI.note: Adv 296/300, @0.050in 222/224, valve lift 13.21/12.62 mm (1.75 ratio; intake/exhaust order not labelled)
